title: Movement of Materials in and out of the cell
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8 Integrated Science; not yet checked by a CBC Integrated Science teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Demonstrations learners can do: a drop of food colour in still water, potato strips in salty and plain water for an hour, raisins soaked overnight, perfume sprayed at the front of the room. Potassium permanganate is handled by the teacher.

skills.key_step: The child says diffusion is particles spreading from where there are many to where there are few, osmosis is water moving through a thin membrane from a weak to a strong solution, and gives their roles in living things (oxygen into blood, water into root hairs).

floor.prerequisite: Knows the parts of a cell, including the membrane.
floor.question: What does the cell membrane do?

representations: a membrane drawn with water arrows
a chart: process, what moves, example in living things
steps: Diffusion: many to few, until even.
Osmosis: water only, through a membrane, weak to strong solution.
In living things: oxygen into blood, carbon dioxide out, water into roots.
contexts: the smell of chapati from the kitchen
oxygen entering blood in the lungs

board.do: Draw a membrane with few dots on one side and many on the other.
Ask which way the dots will spread.
Draw an arrow from many to few.

misconceptions.ask: Where does the perfume smell go: to the back or the front?
misconceptions.repair: Particles spread from many to few.

misconceptions.ask: Does the dye in a glass of water need a living cell to spread?
misconceptions.repair: Diffusion needs no energy from the cell.

misconceptions.ask: How did the smell reach the back of the room?

checks.question: In diffusion, which way do particles move?
checks.answer: from where there are many to where there are few

skills.key_step: The child predicts and explains the result of a simple demonstration (dye spreading, potato strips in salty and plain water, a raisin soaking) by particles spreading or water moving through a membrane.

floor.prerequisite: Knows what diffusion and osmosis are.
floor.question: What moves in osmosis?

representations: dye in hot and cold water
steps: Explain with particles or water moving.
Check the fair test: only one thing changed.

board.do: Draw a potato strip in salty water and one in plain water.
Ask what each strip will be like after an hour.
Draw the salty-water strip shorter and floppy, the plain one firm.

misconceptions.ask: Was the strip lighter or heavier after?
misconceptions.repair: Water left the potato by osmosis.

misconceptions.ask: What did the glass look like after an hour?
What did the soaked raisin look like?
misconceptions.repair: Water moves in, so it swells.

checks.question: A raw potato strip is left in plain water. What happens to it, and why?
checks.answer: it becomes firm and slightly longer, because water moves into it by osmosis

checks.question: Why does tea colour spread faster in hot water?
checks.answer: the particles move faster when hot
